descriptive_reason: No data-value means, dispersions, or percentiles are reported for the variables in the selected Table 4 models. Tables 1–2 describe the literature survey, Table 3 is a first-stage regression, Table 5 partitions samples for further analysis, and Table 6 concerns a different replication study.

results_review_notes: Extraction follows the frozen baseline family: Table 4 column 2; Table 5 endogenous-switching loan and bond columns; Table 6 endogenous-switching loan and bond columns; Table 7 sample-selection loan and bond columns. OLS columns, Table 4 column 3, Table 7 plain probit columns, AQ-quintile low-versus-high hypothesis tests, and correlations are excluded.

Relevant descriptive rows for retained variables are reported in Tables 1–3 and prose. Table 2 Panel D and Table 3 Panel B AQ-quintile means are included; the associated low-versus-high t-test columns are excluded as inference. The paper does not report descriptives for retained Capital Market Access or Asset Maturity; available summary locations were reviewed.

The source defines Not Rated=1 in the absence of a credit rating on page 11, but Appendix A on page 23 defines Not Rated=1 when the firm has a rating; the sign/coding conflict is not resolvable from the paper.

Tables 5–6 identify endogenous switching and report clustered heteroscedasticity-corrected SEs, but do not explicitly name the estimator for the selected continuous-outcome equations. No estimator was inferred.

Tables 6–7 legends as printed show “**, ***” while naming three significance levels (10, 5, 1 percent); threshold mapping is ambiguous. All markers are preserved verbatim, and no marker-derived p bounds are emitted.
Table 7 note says year dummies are included; the page 20 design description says year and loan/bond-purpose dummies are included for Tables 5–7. Both statements are retained.

Tables 5–7 footnotes identify the selection-model specification as specification 2 in Table 3; page 21 prose says the selection model is the same as specification 2 of Table 4. The discrepancy is preserved without changing the selected baseline fits.

Table 2 cells otherwise retain the printed variable-specific Ns and units, but its dollars-in-millions note for ACQ_SIZE and TRG_SIZE conflicts with the Appendix natural-log definitions; TRG_SIZE also has an unresolved target/acquirer referent. The source does not reconcile these mappings.

review_notes: Panel B does not state the scale or units for its annual median acquirer market-value figures; those values are preserved as printed and linked unclearly to the frozen log-size term.
The overall sample (N=1,307) is broader than the Table 3 SYNERGY and ΔROA columns.

variables.name: Median acquirer market value of equity, by announcement year

review_notes: Variable-specific observations are retained exactly as printed. Table 2 uses the full descriptive sample for many controls, so those rows may be broader than the smaller SYNERGY and ΔROA estimation samples.

The frozen specification preserves unresolved source-definition conflicts for ACQ_TOBIN_DUM coding and the TRG_SIZE/TRG_TOBIN referents. Table 2 descriptive rows are linked as unclear where those source conflicts prevent a direct mapping.

Source scale inconsistency: Table 2 notes present ACQ_SIZE and TRG_SIZE in dollars (millions), while Appendix pp.40–41 define both terms as natural logarithms of market value; TRG_SIZE is also labeled as target size but defined using acquirer value. The source does not reconcile these descriptions. Keep the Table 2 cells as printed and retain the raw-version/unclear links without transforming values.

results_review_notes: Confirmed the frozen no_baseline_regression scope: the principal tests are portfolio comparisons in Tables 3–4 (physical PDF pages 16–22) and reversal portfolios in Tables 5–7 (pages 26–40). The table headers and notes describe yearly formed portfolios, their means/medians and Fama–MacBeth statistics; they are not baseline regression result sets.

Equation (3) on page 23 is a cross-sectional return-risk regression used to create abnormal-return residuals reported in portfolio analyses. Endnote 19 (pages 47–48) describes reporting-bias regressions and endnote 20 describes monthly-return regressions; both are supplemental checks and not substitutes for the principal portfolio designs. No baseline model or model-linked descriptive rows are therefore added.
descriptive_reason: No baseline regression is retained for this paper, so there are no retained model variables for related descriptive statistics.

The viewed methods and main-results tables show that the principal family compares analyst FY1/FY2/FY3 forecasts with parameter-free random-walk forecasts and reports mean differences in absolute forecast errors across months and subsamples; these are not fitted regression equations.

The random-walk forecasts use lagged realized annual EPS and are explicitly stated to require no parameter estimates. The FY3 forecast is calculated from FY2 and analysts’ long-term growth, not an estimated regression.

Table 2 reports firm characteristics and signed forecast-error descriptives, not descriptive statistics for variables in a selected baseline regression. No model variables are retained for descriptive linking.

results_review_notes: Only the two frozen Table 5 final full-specification baseline models are retained: quarterly Panel A and annual Panel B, each using the third column. The first two partial-control columns, Table 4 contemporaneous-return tests, Table 6 decompositions and later financing/investment analyses are excluded.

The final selected models contain the three period-aligned breadth changes, the current-period idiosyncratic-risk rank and the three matching breadth-by-risk interactions. No standalone risk main effects at t−1 or t+1 are added; the Table 5 footnote says those are omitted for brevity because risk is highly autocorrelated.

The source labels the statistics t-statistics and states that Newey–West correction with four lags is used. It does not state sidedness or degrees of freedom, so those remain unknown and no p-values are derived.

The within-quarter cross-sectional estimator is not named in the source. The result sets retain mean coefficients across quarterly fits and the reported average cross-section N without treating it as an exact per-fit sample size.

Two Table 5 source conflicts in the frozen base remain unresolved: the size-adjusted-return subtraction direction differs from Section 3, and the Table 5 percentage scaling for breadth conflicts with the main-text proportion definition and coefficient interpretation. No scale/sign correction is made.

The Table 5 note describes size-adjusted return as size-decile portfolio return minus the firm return, while Section 3 on physical page 7 describes firm return minus its size-matched portfolio return. Both source definitions are retained as conflicting; no coefficient sign adjustment is applied.

The Table 5 and Table 3 notes state that percentage breadth is multiplied by 100, while Section 3 defines DBREADTH as a change in the fraction of 13F filers. Coefficients remain on the printed Table 5 scale with multiplier 1; Table 1 descriptive units remain as printed.
Table 3 reports portfolio returns by breadth decile and high-minus-low t tests, rather than data-value summary statistics; it is not added as a variable-descriptive group.

results_review_notes: All 10 selected Table 2 baseline fits, their 117 frozen predictors, intercepts, coefficient estimates and direct p-values, fit-level Wald/LR rows, and fit observation counts are retained. Table 2 does not report coefficient standard errors or identify the fitted quantile.

Table 1 descriptives are retained for 14 matched baseline outcomes and related current-ratio, market-to-book, CFO and assets measures. It reports no values for the other retained controls; non-retained leverage, ROA and debt-size rows are excluded.

Table 1 reports Mean, Q1, Median, and Q3 by CLOSE/DEFAULT/FAR group (Obs.=1,655/2,927/10,234). Those are group Ns, not variable-specific Ns, and the descriptive groups do not equal every complete-case Table 2 fit sample.
Table 2 prints ΔGDP and the clipped Panel B label REMCOMBIN; stable model-local terms are retained by named table row and column. The panel row maps to the specification variable REMCOMBINE.

The paper describes REMCOMBINE as REMPROD minus REMEXP minus REMCFO after reversing the signs of the latter components (p. 11), while Table 6 calls it the sum of the three components (p. 30). Both source statements are preserved.

variables.name: Total Assets
review_notes: Table 1 gives this row as “Total Assets” without stating units or transformation. The paper defines PCOST as the log of book-value total assets (pp. 14, 30); the row is linked to the underlying asset measure, but the descriptive scale relative to PCOST cannot be established, so the relation remains unclear.

variables.name: Current Ratio
review_notes: The printed Table 1 row label is visibly overprinted (“Current Ratio RRRatioRatiRatio”); it is normalized as Current Ratio for linking. variables.name: CFO
review_notes: Linked as an upstream input to the retained REMCFO residual outcome. The paper's Eq. (6) scales CFO by lagged assets, while its prose defines CFO as operating cash flow divided by total assets (p. 11); this source scaling discrepancy is preserved.
